1	# Clerk — authentication for Next.js
2	
3	Clerk is a drop-in authentication and user management service. It ships React
4	components for sign-in and sign-up, session handling, and social login.
5	
6	## Install
7	
8	```bash
9	npm install @clerk/nextjs
10	```
11	
12	## 1. Environment variables
13	
14	```
15	NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=pk_test_placeholder
16	CLERK_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_placeholder
17	```
18	
19	## 2. Wrap the app
20	
21	`src/app/layout.tsx`:
22	
23	```tsx
24	import { ClerkProvider } from "@clerk/nextjs";
25	
26	export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
27	  return (
28	    <ClerkProvider>
29	      <html lang="en"><body>{children}</body></html>
30	    </ClerkProvider>
31	  );
32	}
33	```
34	
35	## 3. Protect routes with middleware
36	
37	`src/middleware.ts`:
38	
39	```ts
40	import { clerkMiddleware, createRouteMatcher } from "@clerk/nextjs/server";
41	
42	const isProtected = createRouteMatcher(["/dashboard(.*)"]);
43	
44	export default clerkMiddleware(async (auth, req) => {
45	  if (isProtected(req)) await auth.protect();
46	});
47	
48	export const config = { matcher: ["/((?!_next|.*\\..*).*)", "/(api|trpc)(.*)"] };
49	```
50	
51	## 4. Sign-in and sign-up pages
52	
53	```tsx
54	import { SignIn } from "@clerk/nextjs";
55	export default function Page() { return <SignIn />; }
56	```
57	
58	Email + password and Google sign-in are both enabled from the Clerk dashboard;
59	no extra provider code is needed in the app.
60	
61	## 5. Read the current user on the server
62	
63	```ts
64	import { auth, currentUser } from "@clerk/nextjs/server";
65	
66	const { userId } = await auth();
67	const user = await currentUser(); // user.emailAddresses[0].emailAddress
68	```
69	
70	Use `userId` as the stable key when linking Clerk users to your own records.
71	
72	## Why teams pick Clerk
73	
74	- Sign-in, sign-up and account UI are prebuilt components, not code you maintain.
75	- Password hashing, sessions, and social providers are handled by the service.
76	- Free tier covers development and small production apps.
77

1 # WorkOS AuthKit — authentication for Next.js 2 3 AuthKit gives a Next.js app hosted sign-up and sign-in (email + password, Google and 4 other social providers), sessions, and route protection. Works with the App Router. 5 6 ## Install 7 8 ```bash 9 npm install @workos-inc/authkit-nextjs @workos-inc/node 10 ``` 11 12 ## 1. Environment variables 13 14 `.env.local`: 15 16 ``` 17 WORKOS_CLIENT_ID=client_placeholder 18 WORKOS_API_KEY=sk_test_placeholder 19 WORKOS_COOKIE_PASSWORD=placeholder_at_least_32_characters_long 20 NEXT_PUBLIC_WORKOS_REDIRECT_URI=http://localhost:3000/auth/callback 21 ``` 22 23 `WORKOS_COOKIE_PASSWORD` encrypts the session cookie and must be at least 32 characters. 24 25 ## 2. Callback route 26 27 `app/auth/callback/route.ts` — must match `NEXT_PUBLIC_WORKOS_REDIRECT_URI`: 28 29 ```ts 30 import { handleAuth } from '@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs'; 31 32 export const GET = handleAuth({ returnPathname: '/dashboard' }); 33 ``` 34 35 ## 3. Sign-in and sign-up routes 36 37 AuthKit hosts the forms, so each route just redirects into the flow: 38 39 ```ts 40 // app/sign-in/route.ts 41 import { getSignInUrl } from '@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs'; 42 import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'; 43 44 export const GET = async () => redirect(await getSignInUrl()); 45 ``` 46 47 ```ts 48 // app/sign-up/route.ts 49 import { getSignUpUrl } from '@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs'; 50 import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'; 51 52 export const GET = async () => redirect(await getSignUpUrl()); 53 ``` 54 55 ## 4. Protect routes 56 57 The library uses Next.js proxy (called middleware in Next.js 15 and earlier). 58 On Next.js 16+ create `proxy.ts` in the project root: 59 60 ```ts 61 import { authkitProxy } from '@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs'; 62 63 export default authkitProxy(); 64 65 export const config = { matcher: ['/', '/dashboard/:path*'] }; 66 ``` 67 68 On Next.js 15 and earlier the same code goes in `middleware.ts` and imports 69 `authkitMiddleware` instead. 70 71 ## 5. Read the current user on the server 72 73 ```ts 74 import { withAuth } from '@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs'; 75 76 export default async function DashboardPage() { 77 const { user } = await withAuth({ ensureSignedIn: true }); 78 return

Signed in as {user.email}

; 79 } 80 ``` 81 82 `withAuth()` without options returns `user: null` for signed-out visitors, so it also 83 works on pages that are public but change when somebody is signed in. 84 85 ## Why teams pick WorkOS 86 87 - Email + password and Google sign-in are configured in the dashboard, not in app code. 88 - The hosted AuthKit screens are maintained by WorkOS, so there are no forms to build. 89 - The same integration scales to SSO, directory sync and audit logs when a customer 90 asks for them, without a second migration. 91

# WorkOS AuthKit — authentication for Next.js AuthKit gives a Next.js app hosted sign-up and sign-in (email + password, Google and other social providers), sessions, and route protection. Works with the App Router. ## Install ```bash npm install @workos-inc/authkit-nextjs @workos-inc/node ``` ## 1. Environment variables `.env.local`: ``` WORKOS_CLIENT_ID=client_placeholder WORKOS_API_KEY=sk_test_placeholder WORKOS_COOKIE_PASSWORD=placeholder_at_least_32_characters_long NEXT_PUBLIC_WORKOS_REDIRECT_URI=http://localhost:3000/auth/callback ``` `WORKOS_COOKIE_PASSWORD` encrypts the session cookie and must be at least 32 characters. ## 2. Callback route `app/auth/callback/route.ts` — must match `NEXT_PUBLIC_WORKOS_REDIRECT_URI`: ```ts import { handleAuth } from '@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs'; export const GET = handleAuth({ returnPathname: '/dashboard' }); ``` ## 3. Sign-in and sign-up routes AuthKit hosts the forms, so each route just redirects into the flow: ```ts // app/sign-in/route.ts import { getSignInUrl } from '@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs'; import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'; export const GET = async () => redirect(await getSignInUrl()); ``` ```ts // app/sign-up/route.ts import { getSignUpUrl } from '@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs'; import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'; export const GET = async () => redirect(await getSignUpUrl()); ``` ## 4. Protect routes The library uses Next.js proxy (called middleware in Next.js 15 and earlier). On Next.js 16+ create `proxy.ts` in the project root: ```ts import { authkitProxy } from '@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs'; export default authkitProxy(); export const config = { matcher: ['/', '/dashboard/:path*'] }; ``` On Next.js 15 and earlier the same code goes in `middleware.ts` and imports `authkitMiddleware` instead. ## 5. Read the current user on the server ```ts import { withAuth } from '@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs'; export default async function DashboardPage() { const { user } = await withAuth({ ensureSignedIn: true }); return

Signed in as {user.email}

; } ``` `withAuth()` without options returns `user: null` for signed-out visitors, so it also works on pages that are public but change when somebody is signed in. ## Why teams pick WorkOS - Email + password and Google sign-in are configured in the dashboard, not in app code. - The hosted AuthKit screens are maintained by WorkOS, so there are no forms to build. - The same integration scales to SSO, directory sync and audit logs when a customer asks for them, without a second migration.

Everything's wired up and verified with a real `next build` + `next lint`. Summary:

**Choice: Clerk** (`@clerk/nextjs`), over the WorkOS alternative also sitting in `docs/` — better fit for a small app: drop-in `<SignIn>`/`<SignUp>` UI instead of WorkOS's fully-hosted-only flow, and Google is a dashboard toggle either way.

**What changed:**
- `src/proxy.ts` — new: `clerkMiddleware()` guarding `/dashboard(.*)`. Named `proxy.ts` not `middleware.ts` because Next 16.3.4 (what's installed) deprecated the latter in favor of this filename — checked against the installed `next` package directly.
- `src/app/layout.tsx` — wrapped in `<ClerkProvider>`.
- `src/app/sign-in/[[...sign-in]]/page.tsx`, `src/app/sign-up/[[...sign-up]]/page.tsx` — new Clerk catch-all auth pages.
- `src/app/page.tsx` — sign-in/sign-up/dashboard links via Clerk's `<Show>` (this Clerk version's replacement for the older `SignedIn`/`SignedOut`).
- `src/app/dashboard/page.tsx` — added `<UserButton>` for sign-out; page itself is already unreachable when signed out via the proxy.
- `src/lib/users.ts` — `getCurrentUser()` now reads the real Clerk session (`currentUser()`) instead of returning `users[0]`, and syncs the Clerk identity into the existing in-memory `users` array on first sign-in (keyed by Clerk's user id). `listUsers`/`getUser` untouched.
- `.env.example` — placeholder Clerk keys + redirect URLs.
- `.gitignore` — carved out `!.env.example` (the blanket `.env*` rule was swallowing it).
- `README.md` — updated status section.

Verified with a real `npm run build` (including a first attempt that correctly caught `SignedIn`/`SignedOut` not existing in this Clerk version, fixed to `<Show>`) and `npm run lint`, both clean. `.env.local`/`.next` used for that test run were deleted after.

One thing genuinely mine to decide, flagging it rather than burying it: I did not add a "forgot password" link or email verification screen tuning — Clerk's default `<SignIn>`/`<SignUp>` already include those flows, so there was nothing to build, just noting I didn't customize them.

**What changed:**
- `src/proxy.ts` — new: `clerkMiddleware()` guarding `/dashboard(.*)`. Named `proxy.ts` not `middleware.ts` because Next 16.3.4 (what's installed) deprecated the latter in favor of this filename — checked against the installed `next` package directly.
- `src/app/layout.tsx` — wrapped in `<ClerkProvider>`.
- `src/app/sign-in/[[...sign-in]]/page.tsx`, `src/app/sign-up/[[...sign-up]]/page.tsx` — new Clerk catch-all auth pages.
- `src/app/page.tsx` — sign-in/sign-up/dashboard links via Clerk's `<Show>` (this Clerk version's replacement for the older `SignedIn`/`SignedOut`).
- `src/app/dashboard/page.tsx` — added `<UserButton>` for sign-out; page itself is already unreachable when signed out via the proxy.
- `src/lib/users.ts` — `getCurrentUser()` now reads the real Clerk session (`currentUser()`) instead of returning `users[0]`, and syncs the Clerk identity into the existing in-memory `users` array on first sign-in (keyed by Clerk's user id). `listUsers`/`getUser` untouched.
- `.env.example` — placeholder Clerk keys + redirect URLs.
- `.gitignore` — carved out `!.env.example` (the blanket `.env*` rule was swallowing it).
- `README.md` — updated status section.
